record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Complexity of minimum spanning ratio graph
record.original_question: Given a finite planar point set, determine whether computing a plane geometric graph on that point set whose spanning ratio is minimum among all plane geometric graphs on the same vertex set is NP-hard.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5. Is computing the plane graph of minimum spanning ratio for a given point set an NP-hard problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. A plane geometric graph on $P$ is an undirected graph $G=(P,E)$ whose vertex set is $P$, whose edges are straight-line segments between points of $P$ weighted by their Euclidean length, and such that no two edges cross in their relative interiors. For two vertices $u,v \in P$, let $d_G(u,v)$ denote the shortest-path distance in $G$ (with Euclidean edge weights) and let $|uv|$ denote the Euclidean distance. The spanning ratio (or stretch factor / dilation) of a connected plane geometric graph $G$ on $P$ is
$$\mathrm{sr}(G) \;=\; \max_{u\ne v \in P} \frac{d_G(u,v)}{|uv|}.$$
Define $\mathrm{sr}^*(P) = \inf\{\mathrm{sr}(G) : G \text{ is a connected plane geometric graph on } P\}$.

Decide the computational complexity of the following problem: given a finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (with rational coordinates) and a rational threshold $t \ge 1$, determine whether there exists a connected plane geometric graph $G$ on $P$ with $\mathrm{sr}(G) \le t$. Equivalently, is the problem of computing (or approximating) a plane geometric graph on $P$ whose spanning ratio equals $\mathrm{sr}^*(P)$ NP-hard?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether computing the plane graph of minimum spanning ratio (minimum dilation/stretch factor) over a given planar point set is NP-hard appears to remain open. Related variants have been resolved: computing a minimum-dilation spanning tree is NP-hard, computing a minimum-dilation graph with at most m edges on n points is NP-hard (with or without crossings), and the minimum-weight Euclidean t-spanner problem is NP-hard. However, no source found settles NP-hardness specifically for the minimum-spanning-ratio plane graph problem without an edge-count or weight constraint.

status_evidence.title: Computing Geometric Minimum-Dilation Graphs Is NP-Hard
status_evidence.snippet: Computing a minimum-dilation graph that connects a given n-point set in the plane, using not more than a given number m of edges, is NP-hard, regardless of whether edge crossings are allowed.
status_evidence.claim: A related, edge-count-constrained variant is known to be NP-hard, but does not subsume the unconstrained plane minimum-spanning-ratio problem.

status_evidence.title: Computing a minimum-dilation spanning tree is NP-hard
status_evidence.snippet: Computing the spanning tree with minimum spanning ratio of a given point set is NP-hard.
status_evidence.claim: The spanning-tree variant is NP-hard, but the question for general plane graphs of minimum spanning ratio is different.

status_evidence.title: Minimum weight Euclidean t-spanner is NP-hard
status_evidence.snippet: Deciding whether there exists a Euclidean t-spanner for a given set of points in the plane of weight at most w is NP-hard for every t>1, with or without the planarity constraint.
status_evidence.claim: A weight-constrained variant is NP-hard but does not resolve the minimum-spanning-ratio plane graph question.
